# Spindle

> Spindle is an evidence-bearing lifecycle and control plane for agent skills. It
> lets users inspect and try exact package bytes before adoption, lease them
> temporarily, compose and verify the effective startup environment, realize
> minimal overlays per agent, evaluate bounded behavioral claims, and update or
> retire only state under exact custody. Open-core Python toolchain; MIT licensed.

For the whole documentation in one file, read the bundle:
[bundle.md](bundle.md).

## Core idea

- The primary UX is harness-native: `spindle harness setup --harness <codex|claude>
  --here` projects a minimal operator invoked as `$spindle` in Codex or
  `/spindle` in Claude Code. It reads current facts and command contracts from
  `spindle harness context`, rather than duplicating a CLI manual in skill prose.
- Installation does not prove intent, authority, activation, compatibility,
  usefulness, or maintenance ownership. Spindle keeps those decisions separate.
- The lifecycle is **inspect → try/borrow → compose → bootstrap → realize →
  activate → evaluate → adopt/update/distill/release/retire**.
- Temporary use comes first: `try` creates one disposable read-only session;
  `borrow` creates an exact expiring lease. Only `adopt` creates durable custody.
- Desired state lives in a content-addressed surface lock. Startup inventories the
  effective harness environment, repairs only receipt-owned drift, preserves
  foreign state, and writes a receipt before task execution.
- Composition still matters: `bind` resolves a tight surface-specific set,
  renders it for the harness/model, verifies guardrails, and records ownership.
- Parent and child agents independently realize and prove their served model,
  tools, policy, and projection. Shared package state is never rewritten to route
  one session.
- Effectiveness is tuple-bound. Named-arm evaluations rebaseline no-skill
  behavior and permit smaller or empty overlays only through held-out
  non-inferiority, hard-floor, runtime, and efficiency gates.

## Vocabulary (quick reference)

- **skill**: a directory with a `SKILL.md` (frontmatter `name`/`description` + body);
  the canonical authored-once unit, kept small.
- **package**: pip project shipping skills, declared with `[tool.spindle.package]`.
- **cache**: immutable package bytes available locally, without runtime or
  maintenance authority.
- **lease**: expiring authority to project exact bytes without durable adoption.
- **activation**: per-agent evidence for the loaded realization, served model,
  tools, and policy.
- **adoption**: durable maintenance custody promoted from a successful trial.
- **distribution**: pip bundle grouping packages + carrying doctrine, channels,
  profiles; declared with `[tool.spindle.distribution]`.
- **channel**: versioned `(scope × harness)` manifest listing which skills a surface
  gets at that scope, plus the absolutes in force.
- **surface**: a repo or agent consuming a blend (name, harness, autonomy, clusters,
  model).
- **profile**: a versioned renderer; a *harness* profile sets dialect, a *model*
  profile sets density. Transforms: `identity`, `terse`, `trim`, `llm`.
- **realization**: one immutable skill package containing the invariant core plus
  at most one overlay selected from an explicit agent-session coordinate.
- **surface lock**: exact desired package/projection identity plus active leases
  and conflict decisions for one repository/harness surface.
- **ownership receipt**: proof that Spindle created one exact projection and may
  reconcile it only while path and target still match.
- **blend / composition**: the resolved subset for one surface + absolutes in force
  + recorded overrides (shadows).
- **doctrine**: the versioned first-principles set (preferences, absolutes,
  meta-principles) skills are checked against.
- **scope**: `system | cluster | repo` — drives selection order and precedence
  (narrow wins), except absolutes, which accumulate.

## Key invariants

- Guardrails only accumulate: absolutes are unioned across all channel layers and
  never dropped by precedence.
- Every `ALWAYS`/`NEVER`/`MUST NOT`/`DO NOT` clause in a skill's source must survive
  rendering, or the bind fails closed (`render.verify_preserved`).
- Availability, activation, routing, authorization, behavior, and adapter
  conformance are distinct. Unknown never becomes success.
- Rendering and binding prove desired availability; only held-out evaluation can
  support an improvement or non-inferiority claim. Development cases never make
  a run promotion-eligible.
- Runtime model matching uses the actually served model. Unknown, mismatched, or
  ambiguous coordinates fall back to the invariant core and record an unresolved
  receipt rather than claiming tuned behavior.
- Everything is content-addressed: rendered skills and binding coordinates are
  hashes of their inputs, so re-binding an unchanged surface is nearly free and
  every past coordinate is a rollback target.
- Spindle mutates or removes only exact receipt-owned state. Foreign directories,
  symlinks, plugins, hooks, and same-name collisions are preserved.

## Source

- Repository: https://github.com/lavallee/spindle
- Reference distribution: `examples/spindle-sample` in the repo.
- License: MIT. An open toolchain for composing agent skills.

## Provenance

This site is an [artoo](https://github.com/lavallee/artoo) artifact, built with the
artoo-kit design system and hand-authored from the Spindle source. It describes
Spindle v0.2; adapter claims remain pinned to the exact builds named in their
certification receipts.
